Alternate screen page built by the room renderer. All 1000 cells are zero at the resident handover and cleared by $52C9–$52D5 before being drawn.
Zero-filled at the resident handover. The gameplay renderer generates columns here through $507E and $51B3. The load path temporarily uses the overlapping first bytes to save zero page.

comments.text: Main loop and timed delays wait until two interrupt ticks have elapsed.
The IRQ entry tests this byte to choose the alternate raster handler path.
Low X bytes for staged sprite slots one through eleven. The raster multiplex routine transfers the selected slot to a VIC sprite X register.
High X bits paired with the staged low positions beginning at $6F. The raster routine assembles the VIC ninth-X register from these values.
Staged sprite Y positions starting with slot one. A zero value keeps an inactive story or gameplay slot above the visible playfield.
The tape initialization clears this byte as KERNAL workspace. In gameplay it lies 16 bytes into the displaced colour strip at $B0, which the scroll loop fills and consumes.
Temporary row of 32 colour cells. The scrolling routine saves the displaced strip at $7A12 and reads it back at $7A5F.
Initial zero byte between the displaced colour row and the scroll state at $F1.
Low byte of the address $0D5D installed by the tape state initializer at $7E73.
High byte of the address $0D5D installed by the tape state initializer at $7E76.
Disable interrupts during initial setup, reset the stack, blank the display and set the video colours. Configure CIA2 and select the VIC bank at $C000 before entering the game's title and play loops.
Five pairs for background registers one and two. Level setup patches the raster handler’s colour operands from this table.

Blank the display and select the level in a normal game. Swap the display glyphs back to their level mode. Reset runtime slots, use the level's resource pointers, then initialise level state and draw the room.
Spin until the raster counter at $54 reaches two, then continue the gameplay update at $054F.
Encoded game-over message record. The visible PETSCII begins at $056D.
Blank the display first. In demo mode return without deducting a life. Otherwise enter the checkpoint restore and life deduction routine.

Subtract the current life cost from $69. If the new value is negative, go to the game-over path. Otherwise blank the screen, retire the object slots and restore the saved position, room and scroll state.
Deduct the current life cost from the remaining life count and branch to game over on a negative result. The following code restores the saved room and position for the retry.
Blank and clear the playfield, draw the game-over message, select the menu glyphs and start tune two. Wait a bounded time or accept fire, then test the score for a place in the table.
Positioned text records for the high score entry screen. They hold the name prompt, five rows of selectable letters and symbols, and the blank 16-character entry field.
Length of the name being entered. The character picker uses it as the insertion index, limits it to sixteen and decrements it on delete.
Column of the selected character. The horizontal joystick branches move it in steps of two and wrap from column $18 to $0E and back.
Row of the selected character. The vertical joystick branches move it in steps of two and wrap between rows eight and sixteen.
Previous picker column, used to restore the colour of the old cursor cells.
Previous picker row, used to select the colour RAM row before erasing the highlight.
Incremented when fire selects character $12. The caller tests this flag to leave the picker.
Score rank chosen by the comparison loop. Multiplying by three selects the packed score and multiplying by sixteen selects the corresponding name.
Exclusive descending source offset for the score shift, then for the name shift. After each record the loop steps down by its record size and stops before copying from this offset.

Compare the three packed decimal score bytes at $6E through $6C against eight existing scores. Return without a new entry if all eight outrank this score. Otherwise save the rank and prepare the name-entry screen.
The high-score path replaces this RTS with LDX immediate to activate the name check. Its restore path writes RTS back.
Dormant entry operands for the name test. The score insertion path installs LDX at $083B and LDA at $083D, producing LDX #$00 and LDA $06CA,X.

XOR the name byte with the keyed byte at $139C,X and compare the result against $0872,X. Score insertion patches $0846 to BNE, so a mismatch branches to the restore code. Completing the loop sets the alternate title state.
The first byte is an RTS while the check is inactive. The score insertion path changes it to LDA #$00 and reaches the opcode-restoration code below.
Restore the dormant LDA slot and the original CMP opcode. Return with both patched entry points set back to RTS.
The sixteen expected XOR results, compared one byte at a time by the name-test loop when the CMP instruction is enabled.
Counts calls to the name-entry poll. On four, the routine clears it and reads the controls.

Count calls and handle input every fourth one. Fire selects the character at the current cursor. The up and down scans change the screen-row cursor in increments of two with wraparound, and the left and right scans do the equivalent for the column.
The name-entry cursor looks up colours from this sequence. Its negative terminator sends the cycling index back to the start.
Index of the current cursor colour. The drawing routine advances it and resets it at the negative table entry.
Use the old cursor row and column to find and restore its colour RAM cells, then highlight the new cursor position.
Return from the name cursor drawing path. The music lookup uses this address as its base and a one-based level index to reach the tune bytes immediately after it.
Five per-level values passed in A to $638C by $09C0 on the normal gameplay path.
Use the current level to look up the tune index at $09BA and call the music initializer. Skip the lookup in demo mode.
Encoded selection menu records. Their visible PETSCII includes the five destination names.
The colour byte of the Headquarters record. Menu setup chooses its value from the unlock flag before the common record reader draws the line.
Keep the initial selection index. The level-finish routine tests whether the first choice was Hyde Park before taking the campaign continuation path.
When nonzero, the select screen recolours the fifth choice and extends the cursor limit. The completion path at $14AD writes this flag before advancing from the fourth level.
Selection cursor's last permitted screen row. The menu changes this value when Headquarters becomes selectable.

Hide the display, clear thirteen sprite enable flags at $43B6–$43C2, then configure the menu limit and the fifth entry's colour from $0A66. Draw the menu and poll input until a fire press selects the cursor's level.
Read joystick two up and down from CIA1 port A. Move the cursor by two rows with a top limit of nine and a bottom limit from $0A67.
Screen column for the new selection marker, loaded as Y in the marker draw.
Screen row of the selected level. The menu updates it and uses the row address tables to position the marker.
Screen column used to erase the old selection marker.
Screen row of the old marker. The redraw uses it to choose the screen and colour rows to erase from.
Use the stored previous and current row indices to address both screen and colour RAM. Clear the old marker and draw the marker for the currently highlighted choice.
Set by the first pause press and cleared after the release and second press. The raster handler reads it.
Outside demo mode and screen transitions, check CIA1 port B. The first matching $7F sets the pause flag, then wait for release and a second matching press before clearing it.
Clear the score and two special-object flags, grant six lives and six units of each ammunition type, and set the panel redraw flags.

Use the selected level to patch both operand pairs that index the object template table and the story-table entry. Patch the raster colours from the level palette list. Reset room and scroll state, set both ammunition counters to six, and request panel refresh.
Remembers the requested glyph bank state so a repeated request can skip the swap.
Set to 112 before exchanging eight bytes at a time between the two font areas. The same byte counts down each completed glyph.
Alternate glyph-exchange entry. When the display mode differs it records the new mode, sets $4BDF and $F000 as the two buffers and jumps to the shared exchange loop.
On a mode change, exchange 112 eight-byte glyphs between $4BDF and $E800. This preserves the level's first 112 patterns while the menu uses the VIC's $E800 character bank.
Working countdown for the copier that transfers 32 characters into each 40-column screen row.
Colour to store for each cell that the menu picture copy writes.
Copy three rows of 32 characters from the source pointer. Advance the screen and colour pointers by 40 each row, writing one constant colour for every character.
First byte of the state mixed with the raster counter. The second half of the routine uses it as an XOR input.
Second byte of the raster mixer state, updated after the first and read by the object code.
Add the current VIC raster and the previous two state bytes into a two-byte evolving value. The second update also XORs the newly written first byte and shifts the result before storing it.
Zero addresses $02 through $FF, preserving the two processor port registers.
Set the processor port direction to $2F and the output byte to $35 for the game mapping.
Mask interrupts, set phase one, install the raster interrupt and unmask interrupts.
Acknowledge the VIC interrupt by decrementing $D019 and return immediately.
Wait for VIC raster line $50. Write the RAM NMI and reset vectors to $0D5C and the IRQ vector to $0DAE. Schedule the VIC raster interrupt at $E5.
Interrupted accumulator saved on entry and restored immediately before returning from the interrupt.
Interrupted X register, saved before the interrupt switches branches and restored on exit.
Interrupted Y register saved at $0DB4 and restored on both raster exit paths.

Save interrupted A, X and Y in $0DA8 through $0DAA. Select the raster handler path using $57. The first path changes screen and character selection in $D018, changes vertical control in $D011, and acknowledges VIC interrupts at $D019.
Increment $54. At count two the handler conditionally runs $1D92 and $74A2, then always runs $2D89 and $4362 on this path.
Immediate operand of the colour-one load at $0E5A. Level setup patches the value from the first byte of each pair at $049A.
Immediate operand for the second background colour. Level setup patches it from $049B indexed by level. The IRQ then selects the level font and restores A, X and Y.
The bottom raster path tests this flag to choose the gameplay panel split that increments the IRQ tick counter.
Acknowledge the VIC interrupt, set the character bank from the display phase, and set vertical control and background colours. The story mode ticks its timer and updates the story sprites.
Selects raster line $B8 in place of $E5 in the split-title path.

In the late raster section, increment the delay counter, start or advance the title tune, and stage the title sprites. Select the $E800 character bank and program the earlier raster line for the next interrupt.
Sixteen entries map a requested sound number to a queue slot. The producer reads this map at $48A1.
Sixteen effect preset indices in queue priority order. After selecting a request the dispatcher reads this table at $0F7D.
Sixteen request flags. The dispatcher scans from slot zero and clears the queue when music is active.
Set by the sound request producer and cleared when the dispatcher accepts an effect. Zero lets the dispatcher return before scanning the queue.
Slot of the most recently accepted effect. With an effect active, the dispatcher compares against this value before replacing it.

On the no-music branch, scan sixteen sound request flags for the first pending entry. Compare the queue index with the active effect's priority before passing the corresponding effect number to the SID effects driver.
Starting with twelve staged slots, use the staged Y coordinates to search the scratch occupancy table on the lower stack page. Assign an available interval before the raster sprite writes.

High byte of the second sprite-pointer store operand. Horizontal and vertical screen-copy routines also carry this address as an initial placeholder until their source is patched. The IRQ code beginning at $1001 publishes a sprite pointer, colour and high X bit, then installs the next IRQ vector or sets the end-of-display raster.

The upper sprite pass installs this address at $FFFE. Save A, X and Y, acknowledge the VIC interrupt and call the next sprite pass. The subroutine saves the original stack pointer and uses a separate stack area for the sprite-slot queue.

Compare the low raster byte minus 22 against the current Y of sprites 5 through 0. Reassign eligible sprites from staged position, shape and colour data until the pass ends or a zero marker ends the stack walk. Update the sprite pointer in both screen pages and the corresponding ninth X bit.
Fill the stack page below $0180 with $FF, reset the free pointer at $03 and park eight hardware sprite pointers at $20 in the $CBF8 table.
Start of the object allocation flags. The allocator checks for a zero byte, and a successful spawn sets the selected entry to one.
Active flags for the upper half of the ordinary slot range. The special-object transition at $3E10 clears its slot here.
Zero leaves the explosive slot free. The placement and sliding paths update it and the active-item loop tests it.
Shot active state set on fire and cleared on object contact or when the shot retires.
Object X positions in viewport pixels. The normal placement path derives X from the low five row bits and the half-cell bit.
X position run beginning at ordinary slot five. The aimed special-object path uses this coordinate in its tile and player contact checks.
Pixel coordinate copied from the player’s X at placement and used as the explosive’s horizontal position in the object-bounds test and the explosive update.
Pixel coordinate compared with the object’s horizontal bounds and advanced by shot motion.
Low bytes of the object viewport-relative Y coordinates. The room spawn path derives this value from the object’s tile column and current scroll position.
Low Y bytes for the upper normal slots. The aimed object overlap test reads the first byte of this run together with its X position.
Low byte of the explosive’s vertical coordinate used in contact tests and changed by the item movement and scrolling paths.
Low byte of the shot’s vertical coordinate used in contact checks and updated when the room scrolls.
Current sprite numbers installed by the object animation interpreter. The movement and drawing paths select a slot by X.
Current sprite numbers for the upper ordinary slots. The aimed-object reset stages sprite $8C at the first slot in this run.
Set to $3A when placing the explosive. This occupies the explosive entry in the slot array beginning at $1254.
The shot start paths initialize this slot byte from the firing direction. Right loads $FD at $3B96 and left loads $FE at $3BA9.
High byte of the object’s viewport-relative vertical position. The motion update adds the sign extension of the vertical displacement and any carry from the low byte.
The fractional byte of vertical position. Falling motion adds its velocity fraction here and carries into the pixel coordinate.
Low bytes of the active shape sequence pointers, installed from template offset five or updated by the shape interpreter.
Upper-slot portion of the active shape-pointer low bytes. The aimed-object setup clears this byte while selecting its shape directly.
Low byte of the explosive's current sprite sequence pointer.
High bytes of the active shape pointers. The sprite decoder skips stream processing if the selected high byte is zero.
Upper ordinary-slot portion of the shape-pointer high bytes. Aiming directly clears the high byte instead of running an animation stream.
High byte of the explosive's active shape stream pointer.
Remaining delay from a sprite hold command. The sprite interpreter decrements a nonzero entry and returns before reading the stream.
Hold countdown for the explosive’s slot in the shared sprite animation interpreter.
Elapsed updates in the selected motion command. The motion decoder resets this count when it reaches the command duration and advances the pointer.
Per-slot mask for collision category and lifecycle state. $2BEF sets bit four and can set bit three according to the placement flags.
Horizontal extent in pixels, initially copied from the first byte of the selected object template.
Vertical extent in pixels, initialized from the second byte of the object template.
Active behavior flags derived from the placement record and the selected object template. The update loop masks or tests individual bits to choose a path.
Behaviour flag bytes from the upper ordinary slots, starting at slot five. Indexed worker routines use this range as part of the array at $12B3.
Low part of the room placement record pointer used when returning a consumed record to the room list.
High part of the placement pointer. The release path checks this byte before accessing the linked room record.
Signed horizontal pixel step calculated by the motion interpreter. The player support tests can use this step as the carrying offset.
Signed vertical pixel step from the motion command’s high nibble. The support test saves it for the player when this object provides a floor.
Replacement behaviour mask loaded from the object template. $2BA5 exchanges this mask with the active one when swapping the streams.
Low byte of the secondary motion pointer, swapped with $1317 by the behaviour change.
High byte of the secondary motion pointer. The object template setup loads it after the low byte.
Low byte of the secondary sprite sequence pointer, exchanged with $126A.
High byte of the secondary shape pointer, used when the active and alternate sequences exchange places.
Low byte of the active motion command pointer. The decoder increments it by two after a command or replaces it when it encounters a zero command.
High byte of the active motion command pointer, combined with its low byte at $1559.
Per-slot base shape used in the special-object animation path. The setup at $3E65 writes sprite $6B for the new slot.
Limit compared with the turn counter in the periodic direction-reversal branch of $2E2F.
Counts updates in the periodic reversal path, returning to zero when the horizontal step changes sign.
Signed pixel byte of the special object’s vertical velocity. The falling branch applies gravity and clamps positive speed at eight.
Fractional velocity byte. The falling branch adds $80 on each update before carrying into the integer velocity.
Signed horizontal pixel step. The direction reversal path replaces $02 with $FE or vice versa.
Contact state read before the special object chooses its next horizontal movement. The vertical integration path clears it before sampling again.
Per-slot state checked before applying the default vertical integration. A nonzero value routes to the update at $32F4.
The movement updater clears this byte before checking contact flags. Levels two and four set different signed values when that contact bit is present, and the shape selector tests its sign.
A nonzero entry selects the falling routine at $13D5. The mode setter at $13AC initializes the flag and velocity.
When nonzero, the special-object update decrements this count and takes the integration path without choosing a fresh horizontal step.
High coordinate byte paired with $1248. Item movement, placement and scrolling propagate carry or borrow into it.
High coordinate byte paired with $1249. The shot setup clears it and increments it when the coordinate addition wraps.
Runtime byte used in the explosive update at $40B3. The later paths at $4110 and $416F write this cell.
Sixteen-byte XOR table used by the name-test routine. It reads one byte for each fixed-width name character.
Mark the special object in X as falling, initialize its vertical velocity to minus five and choose a signed horizontal step based on its current position. Queue sound effect five.

Check the current level and the initial menu choice. A campaign beginning in Hyde Park continues into the next level, including the Mines to Headquarters transition. A separately selected level returns toward the title or completion display.
Write A to the Headquarters menu enable flag at $0A66, then fall through to load the following level.

When the first level choice was Hyde Park, convert unused lives to score in 100,000-point steps, then exhaust the two ammunition counters with their own score increments. Redraw the panel and play an effect between deductions.
Load the slot's motion pointer. A zero opcode transfers to the following word. An ordinary command supplies signed nibbles used to move the object relative to the display.
Camera column plus $25. The object traversal stops at the first record at or above this column.
Room setup sets this around its first object scan. The descriptor path at $167B chooses its room-entry branch while it is nonzero.
Walk the current room's object records. Reject inactive or off-screen entries before creating a runtime object. Use the record's fourth byte to skip its extra four-byte descriptors.
Stores the descriptor-loop boundary used in the X comparisons at $179D and $17BA.
Inspect the count in the low bits of an object's fourth byte. Evaluate the following four-byte descriptors at the current scroll and return carry clear if no descriptor qualifies.
Mask the consumed bit out of the room object number. Types below $72 allocate a normal sprite slot. Types $78 and $7C switch the timed bonus state, and other upper types go to the special-slot path.

Allocate a runtime slot, save the room-record pointer, and use the low seven type bits minus one to look up the object template at $AEE0. Copy the template fields into per-object state, calculate pixel coordinates relative to the scroll, and mark the room record as consumed.
Low address byte of the patched fetch that selects the low byte of an object template pointer.
High operand byte of the LDA that fetches an object template pointer’s low part. Level setup patches this instruction along with the high-part lookup.
Low address byte of the second fetch, which selects the high byte of the template pointer.
High operand byte of the lookup at $187A. Index Y is one byte past the template’s low part, and the resulting pointer high byte goes into $63.
Read the template's size pair into the object slot. Combine the template flags with the placement descriptor, copy the motion and shape pointers, and load the extra state fields.
Low byte of the room exit scan pointer, saved before traversing the records and restored at the end.
High byte restored with the original pointer at the end of room exit scanning.
Zero skips the exit scan. Nonzero selects the exit type compared with the low two bits of the record header.
Working column byte shifted with carries from the position arithmetic before matching the exit's range.
Return immediately unless an exit type is pending. Otherwise save the starting exit-list pointer before comparing the records at $1A79.

Walk four-byte room transfer records until a zero type or a match. The first byte carries the exit type and control flags. On a regular transfer the final pair gives the destination room and the initial scroll column.
Return instruction immediately before the five room counts. The reset path uses its address plus the one-based level number as the lookup.
Low byte of the room index scaled by eight for the directory lookup in the object reset.
High byte of the scaled offset. Adding $A4 forms the directory pointer's high byte.
Count of room lists left to process. The reset routine subtracts one to obtain the current directory index.
Read the room count for the selected level. Use the final pair of each room directory record to locate the object list and clear each object's consumed flag.
Walk a room object list until a zero type. Clear bit seven of each type byte. The low two bits of byte four select the number of extra four-byte descriptors after the header.
Five eight-byte initial state records indexed by level minus one. Bytes zero and one select the room, two and three set scroll position, and four and five set the player coordinates.
Select the level's eight-byte starting record. Copy room, scroll and player coordinates into active state, clear fractional displacement, and open and draw that room.
High byte of the room index. The directory reader shifts it in place with the low byte to produce the eight-byte record offset.
Low byte of the room index before the reader changes it in place to the record offset.
Scroll column for the room entry. Setup adds two before storing it as the camera column.
Entry value staged into $F2 when opening the room; the retry checkpoint saves it before the setup.

Index eight-byte records at $A400 using the room number. The first pair gives an offset from $8A00 to the room's metatile map. The fourth byte contributes the right scroll limit. The final two pairs select the exit and object lists relative to $A400.
Saved horizontal coordinate restored for a room retry. A boundary transition can explicitly set it to zero or $E8.
Saved player vertical coordinate restored to $59 for a room retry.
Saved player shape byte restored to $FB on a room retry.
Saved value of the player's facing state at $FE.
Room-entry backup of $50, restored by the retry path.
Room-entry backup of the fractional vertical speed at $FA.
Room-entry backup of the signed whole-pixel vertical speed at $F9.
Saved $1C84 before scaling the room number for its directory record.
Saved $1C85 before the lookup scales the room number into a byte offset.
Saved fine-scroll value from $1C87 for the room retry.
Saved room-entry column from $1C86 for the retry setup.
Saved copy of the motion state at $1F11, restored on retry.
Save coordinates, direction flags and related movement state into the room retry fields. On the special room path, derive the horizontal value from the transition state.

Start at the room object pointer in $5E/$5F. Advance past records whose column precedes the current scroll, using four bytes for the header and four for each descriptor. Leave the first eligible record or zero terminator in $60/$61.

Clear the pending scroll request, then use the look or movement direction and Rick's horizontal position to request a scroll step or a room-edge check. The horizontal thresholds differ for the two directions.
Eight little-endian addresses for the animated character destinations, eight bytes apart through the top of the $E800 font.
Eight little-endian bases in the animated character table at $A300. Each group reserves 32 bytes for four eight-row frames.
Offset into the selected glyph group. Each frame adds eight bytes and the lookup wraps within the four frames.
Even byte offset into the eight animated-glyph address words. It advances by two after copying one glyph.

While the animation state is active, patch the source and destination operands from the respective eight-entry tables. Copy eight rows to one high character slot and advance the group index. After all eight groups advance the frame by eight bytes modulo 32.
Low part of the indexed source address selected for the current animated-glyph group.
High part of the animated-glyph frame source in the level area. X selects the first of eight glyph rows.
Low part of the writable destination patched from the glyph destination table.

High byte of the self-modifying STA destination in the eight-row character copy. After the copy, advance the group-table index by two. When it wraps at sixteen, advance the frame offset by eight modulo 32.
Amount subtracted from the remaining life count at $0583. The shot path also checks this byte together with $1EFC before entering its update.
Secondary guard tested when $1EFB is zero. When both are zero the shot update branches to $1EF7.
Set by the bonus start object and cleared when the award object collects the remaining value.
Low decimal pair of the timed bonus. The countdown subtracts ten here before borrowing from the middle pair.
Middle decimal pair, initialized to $20 when the bonus starts and transferred to the score adder on collection.
High decimal pair of the bonus. The countdown includes borrow from the two lower pairs.
Selects the alternate player update at $342C and suppresses the ordinary scroll update at $74A9.
The player fall routine sets it after reaching position $F6. The main loop tests it before going through the life-loss path.
Set during new-game initialization and checked by the gameplay sprite staging at $437E.
Sprite X high-bit mask set by sprite staging and ORed into the VIC X high register during the raster paths.
The movement code compares it with the current joystick sample and checks it when selecting a player pose.
Mask written to both VIC sprite expansion registers. The falling transition can set the two upper bits.
The movement code decrements this byte while nonzero. The pose chooser selects shape $0A while it remains set.
Contact sample passed to the rectangle point check via $1F08. The rectangle routine compares it with the two bounds for that axis.
Second point coordinate used by the rectangle check at $25D0 and $25E7.
Direction value set by the left and right motion branches. The shot initializer reads it to choose the velocity sign.
Signed whole-byte component of the explosive slide step. Friction moves this two-byte value towards zero.
Fractional component of the slide step. The friction path adds or subtracts its step here before propagating carry or borrow.
Signed whole-byte part of the explosive movement step used when testing its next contact position.
Fractional part added to the explosive position before the pixel step and contact check.
Signed shot step, initialized to eight or minus eight by the shot launch paths.
Fractional coordinate saved after updating the explosive's sliding position at $42D8.
Nonzero selects player pose $0C and calls the ammunition action routine. Room checkpoints preserve the state.
Set by the level-four branch on a bit-zero surface. The walking pose code uses it to select a phase increment of one.
Set by the level-two bit-zero surface branch. With the Mines flag clear, it selects a walking animation increment of four.
Set by the shot input path and tested to choose player pose $09.
The shot routine sets it from the shot's signed step and uses a nonzero value to suppress a new shot until the latch is cleared.
Selects the pose branch that displays shape $0B while either component of the explosive slide step is nonzero.
Player movement animation phase. The updater advances it by one, two or four, reduces it modulo 40 and divides by four for the pose index.
Ten pose indices for the ordinary movement animation. The phase reader at $3999 points to this table.
Ten pose indices for the branch at $3989. The movement animation selects this table when $FE is set.
Initialise the contact scratch values, derive the relevant tile cells from the supplied coordinates and combine their collision flags from the level flag table.

Configure a character-grid probe from the incoming coordinates. Choose the number of adjacent cells from the low coordinate bits and merge contact flags from the character codes in the scrolling column buffer.
Compare player or object extents using the coordinates and sizes in zero page. Carry reports an overlap to callers.

Convert the trial position to character cells, combining tile flags across adjacent columns. Special cases mask flags according to the vertical step. After the background pass, test nearby objects for a platform contact.
Test the six normal object slots whose active and category flags permit collision. On overlap, keep the highest support surface and save its motion delta for the player.
If tile flag $02 already indicates contact, return. Otherwise test the occupied ordinary slots that have both collision bits set and mark shot contact when the bounding boxes overlap.

Set horizontal displacement to zero, calculate tile indices, read the cell through the column pointer table at $7ECC, and use its value to index the level's flag table at $A000. Store the result at $19.
Derive the tile-column and tile-row indices in $15 and $16 from the coordinate bytes at $10 through $12 and a horizontal displacement in $53. Return the horizontally displaced coordinate in X.
Negative remainder when subtracting four from an explosive coordinate. The bounds routine clamps the coordinate to zero and adds this remainder to the span.

Use the player's position and state to choose collision edges, compare them against the object rectangle in zero page and report overlap through carry. Equal horizontal edges branch out with carry clear.
Choose the shot's collision X from its direction and compare the object rectangle's horizontal and vertical bounds against it. Use both bytes of each vertical coordinate.
Construct the explosive's comparison point from its current slot position and compare the supplied object rectangle against it.

Compare the point in $1F08/$1F09 with the rectangle anchored in $34/$35 and $36. Use the two unsigned X comparisons to reject a point outside the width. Reject the Y test when either the starting high byte or the final high byte is nonzero.
Skip an inactive slot. Compare the other rectangle against the active slot with a fixed horizontal inset of five and width fourteen, and a fixed vertical height of twenty.
Skip an inactive slot, then compare both axes using the slot's stored position and template dimensions. Treat touching horizontal edges as separate.
Clear player action flags, contact and fractional-motion state, and pending room-exit fields before positioning the player in a fresh room.
Cycles from zero through seven. The falling animation chooses shape $1C or $1D from whether the incremented phase reaches four.

Add half a pixel to the low byte of vertical velocity and carry into the signed high byte, clamping downward speed to eight. Add the velocity to the player's Y coordinate and request the life-loss path when the coordinate reaches $F6.

Require the explosive slot at $1230 to be clear and the count at $6A nonzero. Decrement that count, set its display refresh flag, record the player's position and initialise the new item's animation and movement state.

Require a clear fire latch and free shot slot before taking the counter path. Decrement $6B, mark its panel entry dirty, initialise the projectile at the player and choose its signed horizontal step from the facing flag.
Counts calls while the bonus is active and nonzero. At $19 it resets and the routine subtracts ten in BCD.
Check the expected opcode at $0583. When the bonus timer flag is active and the value is nonzero, count calls and subtract ten in decimal mode once the interval elapses.

Dispatch special object types $21, $29 and $2D to their own update. For an object using the general behavior stream, load the pointer from its runtime slot. Zero changes the pointer to the following word. Command $FD optionally queues a sound and advances two bytes.
Exchange the object's active motion and sprite sequence pointers with the alternate pair. Swap the category flags and clear both stream counters before returning.
If the slot is active and linked to a room record, clear the record's consumed bit unless its placement flag requests persistence. Clear the live slot.
Call the sprite sequence interpreter with the current object slot in X and return to the object update path.
Check the signed page of the object Y coordinate, then reject positive-page positions with low byte at least 40. Carry set marks the rejected position.
Require Y high byte zero and Y low byte at least 40 for a carry-clear result. Negative Y pages and positive Y pages take the carry-set path.
Build sprite attributes in zero page from the object slots. Read each selected sprite pointer's colour from $A200 before handing it to the raster routine.
Find a free slot in indices zero through five of the active array at $1226. Return its index in X with carry clear. Set carry if all six slots are occupied.
Look for a free entry in active slots six through nine. Return the index in X with carry clear, or set carry when all four entries are occupied.
Pass each occupied slot of the twelve-entry array to the deactivation routine. Clear the state byte at $3C96 afterwards.
This routine writes one to all twelve entries of the slot-active array at $1226 and returns.
Update active slots six through nine in order. Mix the current raster into the evolving state after each active update, then finish at $33D5.
Dispatch the falling state immediately. Otherwise work through the waiting counter and contact state. For the repeating platform type, count to its period and reverse its signed horizontal step.

Clear the per-slot contact state and scratch displacement. Unless the alternate motion state is set, add half a pixel per update to the vertical velocity and clamp its downward whole-pixel part to eight.
Store $32 as the left bound before checking the special object's overlap with the explosive rectangle.
Check the special object's rectangle against the selected target. On carry set, queue score digits and retire the object. A separate path tests its placement against the player bounds.
First three-state phase, advanced on each animation update and added to the object's base shape on the negative-selector path at $33AF.
Three-state phase advanced on every second wrap of the divider. The nonnegative-selector path adds it to the object's base shape.
Three-state phase advanced when the two-update divider wraps. The contact-dependent path uses it for the moving shape offset.
One-bit phase flipped after the divider wraps. The alternate velocity-dependent shape path adds it to the base plus eight.
Zero exits the standard shape path. A negative value starts the base-shape offset at three instead of zero.
Use the per-slot state and direction to compute a picture index. During movement, use the current animation phase and store the result as the slot's sprite pointer.
A one-bit gate toggled whenever the two-update divider wraps. The second three-state phase advances only when the gate becomes zero.
Two-update counter controlling the slower shape phases and alternators.
Cycle a three-state frame and a two-update divider. At the divider wrap, advance the secondary phase and flip its alternating bit.
Proposed vertical position for collision sampling. Contact branches can replace it with a tile-aligned or otherwise adjusted value.
Fraction of the proposed vertical position after adding the velocity fraction. Cancelling a move can clear it without changing the live position.
Player position plus the signed lateral step. The bounds checks clamp this byte and request a room exit on a boundary crossing.
Signed step added to the player coordinate at $58. The left and right joystick paths supply opposite signs.
Check the special player-state flag. If set, jump directly to falling integration. Otherwise sample the regular controls and update movement.

In live play, copy CIA1 port A into $6F and proceed with that active-low joystick value. In demo mode, a real fire press exits. Otherwise read successive input and duration pairs at $85B2 and use them in place of the joystick value.
Even byte offset into the built-in demo input pairs. After one pair's time expires the reader adds two.
Number of times the current demo input byte has been applied. The reader resets it when it advances to the next pair.

Clear the room transfer request and reset per-tick flags. Separate branches handle special movement states. In the regular path add half a pixel per update to vertical velocity, cap downward velocity at eight pixels, and probe the background before committing position.
Pending whole-pixel launch speed. The launch routine copies it to $F9 before resetting it to minus six on the standard path.
Pending fractional launch speed transferred to $FA by the jump and rebound path.

Copy the preselected signed velocity into the active vertical accumulator and reset the stored launch setting to minus six. Add level- and contact-dependent handling for tile flag bit zero before continuing the joystick and collision tests.
With fire held, joystick up takes the horizontal shot routine and down takes the explosive routine. Left and right use separate attack paths and track the prior joystick byte to suppress repeats.
While down is held, add three quarters of a pixel to the fractional vertical speed and clamp the whole downward speed to four. Prepare the resulting position for the next contact probe.

Test the active-low fire bit and the release latch. Require a nonzero item count at $6B and a free slot at $1231, then decrement the count, signal the display update at $2B and initialise the item position from the player's coordinates.
Flag choosing between the aimed-object reset delay and the movement path. The latter copies it into the object's active slot byte.
Set a twenty-tick timer, then put position and stream pointers from five eight-byte records into the first five object slots. Mark those slots active and reset the sequence counters.
Immediate operand of the LDY at $3C53. The setup saves Y here across its call to the sprite animation interpreter, then uses Y to read the motion pointer and advance to the next eight-byte record.
Flag set by the room path that requests the five-object encounter. The ordinary spawn traversal branches around itself while this encounter is active.
Set after placing the five special slots. The encounter logic uses it to gate their update and avoid setting them up again.
Copy of the first special object's X coordinate, passed to the primary contact test.
Copy of the first special object's Y coordinate used as the primary contact reference.
First special object's X minus $14, used in the secondary contact checks.
First special object's Y plus $18, used with the secondary X coordinate.
Run only while both setup flags are set. Advance motion and animation for the five slots, change six sprite-colour table entries, and update the timed movement sequence.
Set six level sprite colours to white. Decrement the current effect timer and return carry set when it becomes zero.
If the cooldown at $49FE is nonzero, decrement it and return. At zero branch to the aimed-object setup.
Working horizontal target difference used by the direction calculation after converting it to a magnitude.
Working vertical target difference, made nonnegative before selecting the stepping ratio.
The setup stores the horizontal target difference here before converting the working value at $3EB2.
Retains the signed vertical difference after the working byte has been made nonnegative.

Choose the special object's reset position and calculate the signed distance to the player, including the position offsets. Scale both deltas together until the components fit the desired per-update range.
Tick down the current timer and clamp it at zero. Update special slot five's position from the two signed deltas, then test the resulting location against the playfield.
The preceding tile test saves X in the immediate operand at this address. The continuation tests the tile flag and compares the selected object position with the player rectangle.
If the shot slot is active, add its signed horizontal step, clear it when it leaves the screen, and sample the level tile and object contact flags at the new position.
Amount by which the explosive slide's fractional speed approaches zero. The contact-dependent Mines branch doubles it from eight to sixteen.
Counter cleared on entering explosive state two and advanced by that state's update at $4313.
Cycles in five updates during active explosive motion. The wrap path requests effect six.
Skip the routine when slot $1230 is inactive. Select the state-two path when $52 is two. Otherwise advance sprite slot ten's animation and cycle a five-tick effect counter as the item moves.
Position hardware sprites six and seven over the same coordinates, include the ninth X bit and vertical scroll, and select their paired shape indices from the current pose.
First entry in the sprite-slot enable array. The stager also reads this entry directly when handling slot zero.
Slot enable bytes tested in descending slot order. A zero clears the staged Y position and skips the position, shape and colour staging for that slot.
Enable entry at offset four of the scene sprite flags. The alternate scene setup clears this position.
Enable entries at offsets five through eleven. The raster staging loop clears the Y position for a disabled slot.
First X coordinate in the story and title sprite array. The indexed scene movement commands update this table.
Horizontal scene coordinates for slots one through twelve. The staging loop applies its VIC offset before publishing each value.
First Y coordinate in the stage sprite array. Scene and title movement code update its indexed entries.
Vertical scene coordinates for slots one through twelve. The sprite staging loop adds 55 before publishing these positions.
Low bytes of the current motion stream pointers, indexed by story sprite slot. The continuation command can replace this byte.
High bytes of the story motion pointers. The update routine checks for zero here before reading a motion command.
Elapsed updates within each two-byte motion command. Story command ten clears this counter when it installs a new stream.
Low bytes of the sprite shape stream addresses. The animation interpreter advances or rewinds each pointer according to the shape command.
High halves of the sprite shape stream addresses. A zero high byte disables the slot’s shape stream.
Clear thirteen slots of the active flags, motion-pointer high bytes, animation-pointer high bytes and both signed position deltas.

Convert the enabled story objects' local coordinates into hardware sprite position values. Read the current shape for each sprite from RAM near $FFC0 and look up the corresponding colour before staging it.
Per-level bases for the vertical coordinate transform of scene sprite frames at or above $60. Subtract the chosen base, double the result and add it back before staging the VIC position.
Scene number saved by the story entry and used to select its command stream from the level directory.
Preserve the requested scene number. Blank and clear the screen, choose the level's scene data, and index its little-endian sequence pointers. Enter the command interpreter with the selected stream.
Transfer the per-level picture directory pointer into $46 and $47. Set $44 and $45 to the adjacent table of scene command-stream pointers.
Low operand byte of the LDA that fetches the low byte of the picture directory pointer.
High operand byte of the LDA that fetches the low byte of the picture directory pointer.
Low operand byte of the LDX that fetches the high byte of the picture directory pointer.
High byte of the address used by the LDX at $451C. The surrounding code copies the two bytes of the picture directory pointer into $46 and $47.
Patched LDA immediate byte stored in $45 as the high byte of the scene script pointer table.
The patched LDX immediate byte used as the low byte of the story script pointer directory. The preceding LDA supplies its high byte.
Fourteen little-endian dispatch addresses indexed by twice the nonzero story opcode minus two. Commands eleven and twelve have zero addresses in this table.
Column to start writing at in each destination row, taken from byte two of the picture command.
Source column taken from the picture command. The copy restores it at the start of each row.
Width in characters taken from byte six of the command and copied to the inner-loop count each row.
Height supplied in byte seven of the command. The copy decrements it after each row.
Current column in the screen and colour rows. The copier advances it after writing one character and its colour.
Current column in the picture matrix. The copier advances it after reading a character code.
Working count of characters to copy before advancing the picture, screen and colour row pointers.
Return at a zero opcode. Otherwise index the story dispatch table and jump to the handler. The handler advances the pointer by the command's length before dispatching again.
Load the sprite index and its two position bytes, initialise its shape state, and enable the slot.
Clear the active byte for the selected story sprite.
Store the two signed displacement bytes in the RAM arrays at $FFDA and $FFE7, indexed by the sprite number. Clear the slot's motion pointer.
Copy the supplied animation pointer to the selected sprite's state arrays and clear its frame-delay counter.

Command five with a zero picture selects a clear screen. Otherwise look up the picture, skip its eight-byte header, and copy a rectangular window of character bytes into the screen with 32-byte source rows and 40-byte destination rows. Set colour RAM from the indexed colour table.
Select the requested row in screen and colour memory. Write characters starting at the supplied column until $FF. Convert $60 to a comma and set each character's colour to one.
Advance the story stream by two bytes and return to the dispatcher.
The opcode-eight entry skips a command byte and its one argument.
Story command ten selects a sprite slot and installs the next two bytes as its motion stream address. Clear the slot motion timer and advance the script by four bytes.
Skip opcode thirteen and its two-byte argument by adding three to the story stream pointer.
The opcode-fourteen entry advances the story pointer by a single byte.
Repeat the requested number of updates. Each one waits for two interrupt ticks, with a fire shortcut in story sequence zero, then advances each enabled sprite.
Visit the twelve candidate sprite slots, updating motion and frame sequences for the enabled slots.
Follow the motion continuation at a zero command. Otherwise use the update count and displacement nibbles in the next pair to change the selected sprite's position.
Add the saved horizontal and vertical offsets to the story sprite position. Clear the active flag when the updated horizontal byte reaches $F0 or higher.
Read the selected sprite's frame stream. If its delay counter is active, decrement it. Otherwise update its RAM shape index from the next token and advance the stream or dispatch an upper command.
Map the effect number in X to a queue index through $0F24 and set that pending byte at $0F44. Also modify the immediate operands that restore A and Y at return.
Immediate operand used to restore A after queuing the sound request. The routine patches this byte on entry.
Saved Y value held in the immediate operand at $48AC and restored before return.
Saved X in the immediate operand of the final LDX. Callers that need to preserve an object index store it here before selecting the effect in X.
Initial sprite sequence for the explosive slot. The animation loop reads each shape index and rewinds by the word after $FF.
Replacement sequence loaded when the explosive changes state. It alternates shape indices and finishes with a ten-byte rewind.

Five eight-byte special-object records. The initializer reads horizontal position at offset zero, vertical position at offsets two and three, and little-endian sprite and motion pointers at four and six.
All five initial special-object slots share this stream. The interpreter at $1559 reads duration and signed-nibble movement pairs, then the zero command at $494D redirects it to $4911.
Sprite $7B followed by an $FF command that rewinds by one byte.
Sprite $76 followed by an $FF command that returns the sequence to the same shape.
Four two-update holds of sprite $77. The twelve-byte rewind at the end returns to the first hold.
Sprite $78 and a one-byte rewind, selected as the fourth initial special-object sequence.
Alternate sprites $79 and $7A. The rewind argument is two bytes, $02 and $00.
Five four-byte pairs of shape and motion pointers, used when resetting the five special slots at $3E10.
Sprite and sound commands for the first alternate stream. The fourteen-byte rewind returns to its initial $A0 shape. The alternate pointer table also selects entry points within this sequence.

Motion streams addressed by the alternate table. The reader at $1559 takes a duration and packed movement nibbles. Zero takes a little-endian continuation pointer, and $FD is a duration in this format.
Initial delay of $14 set by formation setup and counted down before its movement branch.
Reloaded by the aimed-object reset and movement paths and decremented while the object is active or waiting.
The title renderer copies 96 character codes from here to the primary screen, three 32-character rows at a time, using the fixed colour path.
The first large heading in the high-score view, copied as three rows of 32 character codes using colour two.
The level selector supplies this source to the three-row character and colour blitter.
The lower title graphic occupies three rows of 32 characters. The title handler copies them to $C2D4 and writes the corresponding colours at $DAD4.

Backing store used by the glyph exchange routine at $0C8E. The order of bytes is 112 consecutive eight-byte character shapes. The current screen mode determines whether this copy holds the menu or the level glyphs.
Cleared at the start of the sprite interpreter and incremented after a backward jump. The common result path loads it before returning.
Scratch byte holding the low result during a sequence pointer subtraction. The story interpreter also uses it in its relative backward-jump handler.

Read the sequence pointer from the object slot. If a delay is pending, decrement it. Otherwise consume a sequence byte. Values below $FD are sprite pointers and the three upper values branch into command handling.
High byte of the room map base derived from the directory entry. The column expander adds it to the scaled metatile column.
Low part of the base address to which the column expander adds eight bytes per metatile column.
Camera origin in character columns. Scrolling adjusts it by one and the renderer adds the requested column offset.
Room setup initializes the leftward limit to zero. The scroll routine compares the camera column with this byte before following the left-edge path.
Room setup adds three to descriptor byte three. The scroll routine compares the camera column with this sum at the right edge.
The sum of camera origin and requested offset divided by four. Multiplying it by eight selects a vertical group of metatiles.
Four times the low two bits of the source character column. It selects the four-character strip within a metatile record.
Offset from the camera origin to the column being built. The full redraw iterates from zero and the scroll continuations request the entering edge.

Take the camera's character column plus the requested buffer offset. Divide by four to select a metatile column and use the remainder to select a quarter of each 4 by 4 metatile. Read eight metatile IDs from the room map and expand them into 32 character bytes.
In a normal game, clear the score-dirty flag and draw the six decimal digits by splitting the three packed decimal score bytes. Separate dirty flags lead to the life and ammunition icon updates.
If the life display is dirty, clear the flag and update the six icon cells from the life counter at $69. Clear the unused icons and fill the remaining ones with character $0D.
The nine characters used to replace the normal status panel during demonstration play.
Colours used by the demo panel writer, followed by a negative entry that resets the palette index.
Current offset into the demonstration message colour table. A negative table value resets the offset to zero.
Copy nine characters of the demo message into the panel and use the next colour in its cycling table for all nine cells. Restart the colour index on a negative entry.
Least significant packed decimal pair to add to the score. Its carry feeds the middle pair.
Middle packed decimal pair of the score award, added with carry from the low pair.
Most significant packed decimal pair of the score award, added with carry from the middle pair.
Add the three packed-decimal bytes at $5193 to the score at $6C with carry between bytes. Return to binary mode and request a score redraw.
Preserves the address-ring index across the call to expand each room column.
Page selector adjusted by the display page switcher and used when looking up the active screen page.
Expand forty columns into the column buffer, then copy the displayed characters to both $C004 and $C404 screen pages. Use the level lookup table at $A100 for the colour RAM writes.
Low byte of the indexed address patched before copying one cached room strip into the screen pages.

High byte of the patched LDA operand at $5201. The draw loop copies 32 characters to both screen pages and derives their colours through $A100 unless $51B2 is set. Advance all three output pointers by 40 between rows.
Wait for raster $78, then clear bit four of $D011 to blank the display.
Wait for raster register $78, then set display-enable bit four in VIC control register one.
Copy the active screen page into the inactive one. Each path copies one thousand character bytes in five runs of two hundred.
Clear one thousand cells in each of the two screen pages at $C000 and $C400, blank the panel rows and clear their colour RAM.
Clear a thousand characters on both screen pages and fill a thousand colour cells, in five passes of two hundred cells.
Low byte of the column address being generated. The builder adds $20 after publishing each entry.
High byte of the generated column address, incremented on a carry from advancing the low byte.
Set the start pointer to $7FB2 and write forty little-endian pointers at $7ECC, advancing the target by 32 bytes per column.
Set black border and background, set both shared sprite colours, set colours for sprites five and six, and clear the sprite background priority register.
Clear $54 and wait for two ticks per iteration. Decrement X until it reaches zero.
Clear $54 and wait for two ticks per iteration of X. Return early if bit 4 of $DC00 goes low, indicating joystick 2 fire.

Select one of two screen-row address tables using $F3. The menu record's second byte selects a screen row and the first byte supplies the starting field. A separate pointer at $7F80 selects the corresponding colour row.
Copy $02 through $FF into $7FB4 through $80B1. The streamed loader uses zero page while the saved copy holds the gameplay values.
Restore $02 through $FF from $7FB4 through $80B1 after the loader returns.
High byte of the title dwell counter, advanced on carry from $5489 and tested against two.
Low byte of the title dwell counter, tested for $58 when the high byte is two.
High byte of the display duration counter for the high-score screen.
Low byte tested for $E4 at the end of the high-score display.
Counts complete high-score displays. At two, the title routine checks whether it can start the built-in demo.
Clear and redraw the title view, then poll timer and fire state while updating the title graphics. Its exit paths choose live start or the built-in demo.
Shared title and high-score animation values. The high-score sprite updater treats a negative entry as a respawn marker before reading the next step.
Per-slot indices into the title sprite update table at $552E. The updater increments each corresponding index after fetching its value.
Start of the alternate staged sprite palette. The attract animation uses indexed writes to update its entries.
Script-controlled colours for staged sprite slots starting at one. The staging routine uses these bytes when the alternate palette source is enabled.
Alternate palette entry at offset five, reset to colour $0A by the title animation setup at $56D0.
Alternate palette entry at offset six, reset with the preceding entry by the title animation setup.
Per-slot vertical steps subtracted from the title or high-score sprite positions when the animation updater publishes a new state.
Update six high-score-screen animation slots. A negative shape code resets that slot at a fresh raster-dependent position. Otherwise publish its next sprite value and move it vertically.
Signed vertical steps for the large title actor. The title update restarts at the $80 sentinel.
Signed horizontal steps, one per title update, ending at the $80 loop sentinel.
Offset into the title actor's horizontal step table. The reader loops back to zero at $80.
Offset into the vertical step table, advanced after each addition to the actor's Y position.
Add the next vertical and horizontal table bytes to the title sprite position separately. Reset each table index at its $80 sentinel.
Advance the five title sprite streams. When a stream marker requests a respawn, derive new coordinates from raster-dependent state. Store the current shape or movement data for the next update.
Per-slot indices shared by the main title sprite’s trailing elements. The animation handler indexes the shape and offset tables using these values.
Horizontal offsets subtracted at $570F while placing the title sequence sprite. The same sequence index selects its shape.
Title sequence shape indices read at $56F9. A negative entry takes the end-of-sequence path.
Incremented on each title flying-sprite update. Shifting it three times tests the phase bit for the palette branch.
Wait for the appropriate title state and timer. Copy sections of the title's screen and colour rows by one cell to animate the display.
Even stage value passed between title banner colour and scroll paths. Stage $12 selects the scroll-delay branch.
Nonzero routes the title update directly into the banner colour-fill loop.
Even offset used to choose the next colour RAM row during the banner effect, decremented by two after each row.
Index into the banner's colour sequence. The fill loop advances it and compares the remaining distance against the stage value.
Incremented when the banner reaches stage $12. The scroll proceeds when the count reaches $7C.
Colour sequence read at $5883 for the title display. The final byte is $FF.
Normal entry clears the demo flag and menu timer. The entry at $58D7 also clears the timer and sets the demo flag instead.
Nonzero means the fire reader waits for release before reporting any further button press in carry.
Check joystick 2 fire through bit 4 of $DC00. If the release latch is set, clear it when fire is released and report carry clear. With the latch clear, report a press by returning carry set.
Stored match for the title port B key. $5921 initializes it and the key reader clears it after release.
Read CIA1 port B and report an armed $EF test in carry. A latched key waits until the port no longer matches $EF, then clears its latch and returns carry clear.
Read joystick two fire and the CIA1 port B value, and store the respective held-state tests at $58E1 and $5901.
Single positioned text record for the start prompt, with column eleven, row 23 and colour one. The title setup passes it to the menu record reader at $83FA.
Reset title counters and sprite priority, draw the fire prompt and title art, seed the moving title sprites and clear their update counters.
Selects the alternate sprite colours at $4465. The title setup clears it and the high-score display sets it.
Display records behind the high-score view, with row and column headers, colour and space-filled fields. The high-score view fills the scoreboard cells before it draws these records.
Eight three-byte packed-decimal high scores, most significant byte first. The insertion code moves existing scores down in steps of three, and the formatter emits six digits from each entry.
Eight fixed-width 16-byte name entries. The high-score insertion code copies names down in 16-byte steps and writes the new entry from the buffer at $06CA.
Reset the title screen state and render the score table. Draw the heading and initialize the attract sprites while the table is visible.
Eight little-endian destinations for name fields. The high-score publisher patches the screen text from the table of fixed-width names.
Eight little-endian destinations for score digits. The formatter writes decimal character codes to the selected record.
Working record number for formatting high scores. Twice this value addresses the row pointer and three times selects the packed score.
Iterate over the eight scores, select each row's screen pointer and split each packed decimal score byte into two character digits.
Enables the music tick and keeps the queued effects dispatcher off the shared SID path while a tune is active.
Holds the five-bit playlist command argument during dispatch. Pitch modulation and control handlers reuse this byte for their arithmetic.
The sequencer sets this offset to zero, seven or fourteen to select a channel's SID shadow registers.
Current channel index for the note clock and other per-channel state arrays.
The position of the next byte in each music channel’s playlist. The command reader advances it after every direct fetch.
The channel’s playlist-supplied note adjustment. The note reader adds it before looking up the oscillator frequency.
The note or command offset within each selected pattern. Loading or repeating a pattern resets its offset to zero.
Offset into the six-byte playlist rows. The driver uses it for all three channel pointers and tests it before updating voice three.
Music voice 1 shadow holding the low byte of the SID oscillator frequency for the SID register flush.
Music voice 1 shadow holding the high byte of the SID oscillator frequency for the SID register flush.
Music voice 1 shadow holding the low byte of the SID pulse width for the SID register flush.
Music voice 1 shadow holding the high nibble of the SID pulse width for the SID register flush.
Music voice 1 shadow holding the oscillator waveform, gate and other SID control bits for the SID register flush.
Music voice 1 shadow holding the two SID attack and decay nibbles for the SID register flush.
Music voice 1 shadow holding the two SID sustain and release nibbles for the SID register flush.
Music voice 2 shadow holding the low byte of the SID oscillator frequency for the SID register flush.
Music voice 2 shadow holding the high byte of the SID oscillator frequency for the SID register flush.
Music voice 2 shadow holding the low byte of the SID pulse width for the SID register flush.
Music voice 2 shadow holding the high nibble of the SID pulse width for the SID register flush.
Music voice 2 shadow holding the oscillator waveform, gate and other SID control bits for the SID register flush.
Music voice 2 shadow holding the two SID attack and decay nibbles for the SID register flush.
Music voice 2 shadow holding the two SID sustain and release nibbles for the SID register flush.
Music voice 3 shadow holding the low byte of the SID oscillator frequency for the SID register flush.
Music voice 3 shadow holding the high byte of the SID oscillator frequency for the SID register flush.
Music voice 3 shadow holding the low byte of the SID pulse width for the SID register flush.
Music voice 3 shadow holding the high nibble of the SID pulse width for the SID register flush.
Music voice 3 shadow holding the oscillator waveform, gate and other SID control bits for the SID register flush.
Music voice 3 shadow holding the two SID attack and decay nibbles for the SID register flush.
Music voice 3 shadow holding the two SID sustain and release nibbles for the SID register flush.
Shadow value written to the SID mode and volume register after the music voice registers.
Number of extra repeats of the selected pattern. A pattern end decrements a nonzero count and resets the pattern offset.
Remaining note count for voice one. The tick path checks for one and clears it when scheduling an expired note.
Remaining note count for voice two at the second entry of the indexed note clock table.
Remaining note count for voice three. Expiry also clears its skip flag at $5D3D.
Instrument preset byte compared with the remaining note time in $60EA. At equality the voice gate is cleared.
Instrument preset low nibble. Zero skips the pulse modulation path, and a nonzero value sets the threshold for a new pulse step.
Instrument preset high nibble used as the index base for the voice pulse modulation stream.
Playlist-controlled offset added to the low oscillator-frequency byte, with carry propagated to the high byte.
The pitch adjustment step reader tests this wait value before taking another modulation byte. A nonnegative nonzero value counts down.
Index into the pitch adjustment table, selected by the instrument. Zero bypasses the adjustment loop.
Phase of the pitch adjustment sequence. Low bits index its table, and bit seven changes the sign of the adjustment on alternating passes.
Instrument’s base for the voice-control sequence. Zero skips this sequence during note setup and update.
Position relative to the current voice-control sequence base. The updater advances it after applying the corresponding control change.
Countdown until the next voice-control change, derived from the high nibble of a sequence byte.
Pattern command selects this eight-byte arpeggio table offset by shifting the low four bits left three places.
Ticks of the current frequency-slide phase. Zero skips the slide and $FF leaves the count held.
Low byte of the oscillator increment or decrement specified by the pitch-slide command.
High byte paired with the slide step. The slide path includes carry or borrow from the low-byte step.
Countdown initialized from the low five bits of the slide command. The driver waits until it reaches zero before applying the slide.
Saved slide command. Bit five chooses subtraction or addition when the slide is active.
Voice one's shadow-register write is skipped when this byte is nonzero.
Voice two's output skips its register writes while this byte is nonzero.
Voice three's output path first checks this flag before applying the playlist row limit.
Current arpeggio step. Its terminal state determines whether the pitch returns to the unshifted note or the sequence restarts.
Remaining delay before the next arpeggio pitch change, loaded from packed bits of the sequence byte.
Update counter for pulse modulation. It restarts when a new target pulse value is loaded.
Amount added to or subtracted from the low pulse-width byte during pulse modulation.
Relative position in the pulse modulation stream with direction encoded in bit seven. The reader masks it before looking up the current target.
The transposed note-table index saved at note start and reused when the arpeggio adds its offset.
Incremented for each note count expiring in the current pass. The output path clears it and returns without a register flush when it is nonzero.
Return when the music flag is clear. Count down the three channel durations, mark each expired channel for new sequence data, and proceed through the channel state to the SID register updates.

Copy the music voice shadow registers into the SID. Each per-voice control flag can skip a block of writes. The first block writes frequency, pulse width, control and the envelope values for voice one.
While the playlist is active, check the channel countdown. A nonzero value follows the sustain and modulation path. Zero resets the completed effect countdown and fetches the next pattern byte.
Read the current pattern byte using the selected channel pointer. At $FF either restart a repeated pattern or read the next playlist entry. A playlist $FF ends the channel.
Low operand byte of the fetch that takes the next command at the current channel playlist offset.
High byte of the LDA operand at $5F03, set by the tune player for each channel. The continuation advances the playlist position and handles the end token by silencing all three SID voices.
Patched displacement byte of the branch that dispatches playlist control classes to the following jump entries.
Jump to the loader for the next channel value when playlist dispatch selects command class $80.
Three jump stubs selected by the patched branch at $5F33. The targets handle playlist commands for pattern repeat, pitch adjustment and instrument mapping.
Use the pattern number to load a low byte from $6A1C and a high byte from $6A52. Reset the selected channel's pattern state before fetching from that address.
Distinguish note bytes from command bytes. Command $A0 consumes a duration and clears the selected SID voice control. Higher commands branch into duration and instrument handling.
Patched to zero, eight or sixteen for the three music channels. Added to the command nibble to select an entry in the current channel’s instrument map.
Look up the current instrument entry. Copy its pulse, control and envelope bytes into the voice shadow registers and set the channel's effect counters.
Add the channel transposition and note-base bias, then select frequency low and high bytes before applying channel offsets.
Choose the waveform, set its gate bit, mark the note active, and initialise the effect counters from the channel state.
Scale the tune number in A by six to select three two-byte entries. Clear the voice controls and set up the three stream pointers and channel state before playback.
Read the next playlist byte, advance its index and save the byte in the channel pitch-adjustment array at $5D14 before returning to playlist dispatch.
Take the next playlist byte using the channel offset, advance that offset and store the value in the channel state at $5CE2 before continuing.
Low byte of the source address patched into the channel value fetch at $63F9.

Add the channel instrument-map offset to the playlist command index. Read the next playlist byte and save it at the resulting offset from $69EC, then resume the playlist.
Store the playlist command argument minus one in the channel repeat counter, then resume decoding the playlist.
Read the byte at the current pattern index, selecting the pointer at $4A, $4C or $4E from the channel number in X. Return the byte in A.

Note and command streams addressed by the split pointer table at $6A1C. Each channel reads through its selected pointer and stops or repeats the pattern on $FF. Certain pattern numbers share a suffix.
Eleven six-byte rows. Each row holds three little-endian channel playlist addresses. The update routine patches its playlist readers from the row selected by the tune number.

Per-channel playlists selected by the directory at $6701. Values below $80 select patterns. Other values select playlist commands, with $FF ending playback. The row at $6743 is an immediate terminator shared by three channels.

Three sets of eight bytes for the note pitch sequence. The reader at $6317 takes a delay from the low three bits and uses the upper bits to offset the note-frequency index. The first byte of a set also specifies its step limit and whether it repeats.
The lookup at $6036 uses the transposed note index to select a frequency low byte.
The matching high-byte table at $6040 provides the other byte of the same SID frequency word.
Values used by the music pulse modulation path. The low nibble supplies the comparison target for the voice pulse width.
Byte values used to configure the current music channel effect parameter. The note and effect handlers index this data before updating the channel.

Control values indexed from $6991 are combined with the gate bit before writing the current voice. The sequencer reads packed modulation and control selection bytes through the overlapping bases $6994 and $6995.
Seven nine-byte instrument presets. The command reader at $5FD1 translates the instrument number into a preset offset, then reads settings including voice control, envelope and modulation fields.

Three copies of the eight default offsets. Tune initialization copies this table to the writable maps at $69EC.
Low and high halves of the 54-entry pattern address table. $5F44 uses one index for both halves.
High half of the pattern directory. The same index picks a low byte at $6A1C and a high byte here.
Pointer table indexed by double the requested effect number. The effect initializer patches its source operands from this address.
Second byte of the first word in the effect directory. The indexed reader loads this byte and its successors at two-byte strides to patch the high part of each preset pointer.
Zero byte between the last effect-table address and the active-effect byte at $6AAF.
Effect number copied from the request when the preset is selected and cleared when both effect voices have finished.
Request flag read by the effect dispatcher and cleared when the driver accepts the request or continues an effect already in progress.
Requested effect index. The preset selector doubles this number to fetch its little-endian pointer.
Write zero to offsets $1C down to zero of the SID bank and then set the volume register to fifteen.
Copy the requested effect index to the active-effect byte and patch the two preset read operands from the pointer table.
Low operand byte of the first preset copy, which stages offsets zero through $19.
High byte of the patched source at $6AF8. Copy the 26-byte leading part of the requested effect record before handing off to the effect driver.
Copy the 64-byte preset into the voice and filter workspace, then set the two SID envelopes and prepare timers and filter registers.
Low operand byte of the preset read that stages offsets $1A through $3F.

Start a pending sound effect, process a queued effect change, or advance the active effect using its envelope and duration counters. Stop when both active channel flags reach zero.
When channel flag bit five is set, compare the step delay against its counter. At a match, reset the counter and fetch the next control value from this channel’s preset sequence.
Low operand byte patched with the address of the next-offset test. The shared voice path adds its voice offset to $5A.
