High part of the current pitch offset read. It includes the carry from adding the voice offset.
Use the channel's wait counter and direction timer to decide whether to advance its modulation accumulator. Add or subtract the configured two-byte step.
Low operand byte of the read that tests the next pulse command for a nonzero high nibble.
High byte of the patched pulse-sequence read at $6E4B. The sequence’s upper nibble controls continuation. Its lower nibble is copied to the pulse step state.
Low operand byte used to read the current pulse command and extract the next high pulse-width nibble.
High byte of the patched pulse-step read at $6E8A. Store its low nibble as the pulse step and reload the countdown. Later tests age the channel’s output and select its note-offset command.
Low address byte of the read that decides whether another packed waveform command is available.
High byte of the patched pitch-sequence read at $6ED3. The continuation tests the command’s high nibble, advancing the slot or wrapping to its first pitch step when the preset flags permit.
Low operand byte of the read whose high nibble reloads the waveform delay.
High byte of the LDA at $6F05. The routine patches it to read this voice’s pitch command, then stores the command high nibble in its pitch delay.
Low address byte for the current packed waveform byte. Its low nibble selects a SID control value.
High byte of the patched read that takes the current control command. The following instructions extract its low nibble into the voice control index.
Set by effect setup and tested by the update path. The driver clears it when both voice duration counts are zero.
Live voice-one flags copied from the preset. Bits $20, $40 and $80 select pitch sequencing and pulse and waveform looping.
Low byte of the accumulated filter sweep offset, added to the preset cutoff before staging its SID value.
High byte of the accumulated filter sweep offset, updated with carry or borrow from the low-byte operation.
Low byte of the cutoff sum. It is written to the low SID cutoff register and also participates in the high cutoff calculation.
High byte of the cutoff sum, temporarily shifted into the low byte to calculate the value for the high SID cutoff register.
Countdown for switching the filter sweep direction. It reloads from the period when it becomes negative.
Direction flag inverted at the end of a filter sweep countdown. Zero selects addition and a nonzero value selects subtraction.

Starting pitch offset in note-table entries. The sequence reader adds the selected offset to the base note before reading the frequency table.
Next two pitch offsets. At $6D8D the reader checks the next byte for zero before advancing the sequence index.
Last three pitch-offset bytes before the sequence timing field. The indexed read at $6DC1 loads the selected offset.
The pitch sequence advances when its elapsed counter matches this preset byte.

Packed sustain and release nibbles copied directly to the voice-two SID envelope register.
Voice-two gate count, pitch sweep delay, and low and high pitch sweep step. The shared channel routine uses the voice-one field addresses with X set to $30.
Reload for the voice-two pitch sweep direction countdown. A zero value selects a one-direction sweep.
Four packed commands for voice two. Each low nibble selects a SID control value and the high nibble supplies its delay.
Preset byte split into the voice-two pulse update count and the low-nibble pulse target when the effect starts.
The filter setup shifts this preset byte left four bits for the resonance register and ORs it with $0F for the mode and volume register.
Low byte of the base cutoff value. The filter update adds the accumulated offset before writing the two SID cutoff registers.
High byte of the base cutoff value. The filter update includes carry from the low-byte sum.
The filter update decrements this count before it begins changing the accumulated cutoff offset.
Low byte of the cutoff step the driver adds or subtracts from the accumulated cutoff offset.
High byte of the cutoff step. The filter calculation includes carry or borrow from the low-byte change.
Nonzero values set the period for changing the filter sweep direction. Zero selects repeated addition.
Bit seven enables filter setup and cutoff updates. When clear, the initializer writes zero to the SID resonance and routing register.
Copied to $6F30 before the first voice update. The driver checks its bits to select the pitch sequence and the pulse and waveform loops.
The first byte is copied to $6F60 before the second voice update. It controls the same pitch sequence, pulse and waveform paths as the first voice flags.
A leading-half copy sets this flag. The dispatcher checks it to copy the trailing half and finish the effect setup.
Waveform and control values selected by the effect driver. The driver ORs the table byte with the current gate byte before writing SID control.
High bytes of 96 base oscillator frequencies used by the sound-effect driver. The phase step adds a signed offset and carries in the low-byte addition.
Matching low bytes of the sound-effect oscillator table. The per-voice note and modulation sum selects one 16-bit frequency.
Decrement the voice-three timer when it is nonnegative. When the counter becomes negative, zero the six SID registers from $D40E through $D413.
When the trigger byte $709E is negative, clear voice three envelopes, load frequency $1388 and write gated noise control $81. Set the timer to four.
A negative value enables the noise start path. Starting the noise sets this counter to four and the tick clears the voice registers when it underflows.

Signed camera direction retained while the player is within the scroll thresholds. Reaching a room edge clears it.
Set when the camera cannot advance past the right column limit. The scroll update tests it before switching the screen page.
Set by the camera's left-edge comparisons and tested alongside the right-limit flag.

Skip the regular scroll update in special movement states. Copy the requested direction into the active scroll byte. At the coarse scroll transition flip bit four of $F3 to switch the VIC screen page.

Jump directly to the shared return when this dispatch path needs no coordinate update. The entry at $74E2 checks for scroll stage four and switches the displayed screen page before adjusting object positions.
Shift the shot position by the coarse scroll displacement, and adjust its high coordinate byte on borrow.
Adjust the fine vertical offset for the selected direction. When it crosses a character boundary, move player and object positions by one eight-pixel row and schedule the screen-memory copies.
Low byte of the address installed by the scroll scheduler and read by its indirect continuation jumps.
High byte set with the low byte by each scroll scheduler branch.
Four continuation pointers selected by twice the scroll stage when the first path sees a negative direction byte.
High byte of the first of four interleaved little-endian continuation pointers starting at $7612. The load at $7668 adds twice the stage index to read the corresponding high byte.
Four continuation pointers selected on the first dispatch when the direction byte has bit seven clear.
High byte of the first of four interleaved little-endian continuation pointers starting at $761A. The load at $7659 adds twice the stage index to read the corresponding high byte.
Second dispatch pointer table for the negative direction branch at $7683.

Second dispatch pointer table for the nonnegative direction branch at $7670.
High byte of the first of four interleaved little-endian continuation pointers starting at $762A. The load at $767B adds twice the stage index to read the corresponding high byte.
Use current scroll state, screen page and signed direction to select a continuation table. Dispatch through a RAM pointer so each phase runs the appropriate screen copy.
Increment scroll stage $F8 before clearing the continuation guard at $7694. The dispatcher at $7640 installs $7692 in the continuation vector.
Clear guard byte $F4 and return from the scroll continuation.
Select the banked screen page and vertical scroll direction. Install a series of continuations through the RAM pointer at $7610, interleaving copies of screen rows and colour rows.
Continue the pending raster scroll update through indexed row copies. The final continuation stores four in $F8 and returns.
While scrolling is active, move 32 colour cells per affected row upward or downward according to the selected raster scroll path. Preserve the displaced strips in zero page for later rows.
Use the saved row's character codes to regenerate per-cell colours from $A100. Copy the row back into colour RAM and realign the object-list cursor to the scroll.
Low operand byte for the character read used to rebuild the entering colour strip at $D804.
High operand byte of the character source for the first strip colour loop.
Translate the character in A to its colour-table index, write the corresponding colour cell, and work backward along the new strip.
Low operand byte for the character read in the alternate colour strip path at $7B78.
High operand byte of the character source at $7B78. The loop converts 32 characters to colours through $A100 before realigning the room’s object cursor.
Rotate the column-pointer list left by one entry, recycle the old first column, and decode the new column at the far screen edge. Copy a strip to the target screen page.
Low address byte selecting the cached strip copied to $C374 on the first screen page.
High byte of the patched column cache source used to draw the entering strip into the first screen page. After the copy the routine increments the logical scroll column.
Rotate the column-pointer table and generate the rightmost column, then use the alternate VIC screen-page destination.
Low address byte selecting the cached strip copied to $C774 on the alternate screen page.
High byte of the alternate screen-page copy source. The loop writes 32 bytes to the strip at $C774, then increments the logical scroll column.
Decrement the screen column and rotate the column pointers toward the right. Reuse the final pointer on the left, expand column zero and copy data into the first target screen page.
Low address byte of the cache pointer for the entering character strip at $C004.
High byte of the patched cache-column source. The loop copies the first entering strip to $C004.
Rotate the columns right, expand the new first column and copy it into the second screen page.
Low address byte of the cache pointer for the entering character strip at $C404.
High byte of the alternate copy’s patched source. Its destination strip begins at $C404.
The retained tape-prompt selector passes this address to the text renderer. Its first byte is $01 and the disk loader instructions follow immediately at $7CC0.

Turn off VIC interrupts and change processor-port mapping for the ROM routines. Form the second digit of the disk filename from $7D49. Set logical file 1, device 8, secondary address 1, hand the filename to SETNAM, and call the streamed depacker at $88A7.
Filename with a fixed leading zero, a level digit written by $7CDA, and the suffix .R2 followed by an asterisk. SETNAM is called with a length of seven.
The loader overwrites this PETSCII digit before SETNAM so the wildcard filename can select the numbered overlay.
Tail of the filename pattern used by the resident disk loader. The seven-byte source passed to SETNAM includes the asterisk and following terminator.
Level number associated with the loaded graphics and level data. The loader updates it on the paths that install a level.
Level number saved from A on entry to the loader, used when choosing the disk filename and updating the loaded level number.
Disable interrupts before entering the level load path at the following instruction.
Store A as the requested level. Set the RAM hardware IRQ vector to $0D5D, disable sprites, reset $F3, then call the level loader at $7CC0 after the display preparation calls.
Bytes $00,$12 between the disk loader return and the duplicate loader finish sequence.
Second copy of the loader finish sequence. Clear the raster phase, reset IRQ state, enable all eight sprites and publish the selected level before returning.
Bank out I/O and copy 24 pages from $8A00 through $A1FF into $D800 through $EFFF. The high bytes of the two absolute indexed operands advance after each page. Restore port $35.
High operand byte of the tape graphics copy LDA. The loop increments it once per completed 256-byte source page.
High byte of the copy store at $7DC0. With I/O banked out, the setup starts at $D800, advances one page at a time, and stops once the destination reaches $F000.
Choose the message for an initial tape request or for the direction to rewind. Pass the selected text record to the menu text renderer.
Store $0D5D in the vector at $03FE/$03FF, set the tape buffer pointer to $0154, and clear the I/O status and tape transfer workspace used by this loader.
Ten little-endian filename pointers. The tape-loading code indexes the first or second five according to the requested level and whether it is loading graphics or map data.
Ten four-character names. The first five name the graphics files and the next five name the map files.
Forty little-endian column-buffer addresses. The game builds the ring from $7FB2 and rotates it as input scrolls the playfield.
Twenty-five little-endian row addresses for the first screen page. Menu and scene text draw through this table.
Twenty-five addresses for the other screen page. The same writer chooses this table when the $F3 screen-page flag is set.
Twenty-five colour RAM row addresses. The menu and scene routines index this table beside the screen row table.
Base of the RAM column cache. The renderer lays out forty consecutive 32-character columns and rotates their pointers on horizontal scrolling. The loader reuses the low end to preserve zero page.
Character-indexed colour values used by the story picture copier. The copier writes the map character first, then reads the matching colour from this table.
Attract-mode input sequence. $343D reads each pair as an active-low virtual joystick byte and the duration to hold it. A real fire press exits this path.
Five little-endian template directory bases, one per level. Initialization patches the template address operands used to spawn objects.
One little-endian story directory base per level. Initialization uses each base to locate the scene picture directory and the story command streams.
Stored PETSCII message at the end of the resident engine. The visible text marks the code end.

Read a variable-length bit selector. One path reads literal bytes from the serial stream and writes them backward. The other decodes a distance and copies from the already emitted region. Both update the descending output pointer before the next command.
Shift X bits from the $FB selector buffer into A and $A7. If the sentinel shifts out, refill, resume the same shift loop and return with X set to two.
Read another streamed byte, rotate in a sentinel bit and use the result to refill the selector shift register at $FB.
Writable opcode after the bit-buffer refill. It is RTS in the gameplay snapshot. The related entry at $8823 stores $4C here to select the following absolute jump operand.
Fixed address operand $881A for the JMP form installed at $8834 by the refill entry at $8823.
One $EA byte between the refill exit operand and the loader unwind at $8838.
Pull five bytes from the stack, then return from the exhausted read path. The branch from $889A reaches this when the decremented remaining-byte count underflows.
Two $EA bytes after the loader unwind return and before the selector reader at $8840.
Shift the buffered selector byte left. Refill the buffer when the sentinel shifts out, otherwise return the extracted bit in carry.
Subtract the offset at $A8 from the low byte of the backward output pointer and borrow from the high byte as needed.
Set device eight and the secondary address, open the named file through the KERNAL, and address the drive and channel for the streamed read.
Read five serial bytes into $FB through $FF. Clear the scratch byte at $A9 and bank out ROM and I/O before entering the decoder.
Bank in I/O and ROM while reading the serial byte, with mirrored VIC writes changing the visible stripes. Bank out I/O before returning to the depacker's RAM stores.

Immediate operand of the LDA at $887F. The byte is written through a border register mirror and decremented. The reader decrements its byte limit, unwinds at exhaustion, or gets the next serial byte and switches back to RAM.

Save the processor port and border colour before calling the disk receive and unpack logic. Wait for the serial status byte to indicate end of file, close the transfer through ROM, and restore the saved border and port.

The screen clearer zeroes this forty-byte row before the panel is drawn. In the VIC bank the same bytes also lie inside the sprite graphics address space.
Runtime status text and icon strip. The score formatter writes from $CB9C, and the life and ammunition handlers write or clear adjacent glyphs.

Start of the screen cells overwritten with the nine demonstration message characters by $516C.
Base of the six shot icon cells. Indexed stores write blank glyphs above the remaining ammunition count and the shot glyph for available shots.
The life redraw loop uses the six cells after this address, writing character $0D for remaining lives and zero for unused cells.
Eight sprite pointer slots for the panel screen at $C800. Raster setup initializes them to the blank VIC sprite at slot $20.
More resident VIC sprite patterns in the bank at $C000. These advance the sprite pointer index from $30 to $3F.
Shapes at sprite indices $40 through $4F in the bank at $C000. This RAM lies under the I/O registers in the CPU map.
Resident shape patterns at sprite indices $50 through $5F in the bank at $C000. The VIC can fetch them while the CPU sees I/O.
First half of the shared character generator. The IRQ sets the character bits of $D018 to $0C, selecting $F000 in the VIC bank at $C000.
Upper character codes use the second half of the glyph table starting at $F000. Each code selects eight rows.
Shared VIC graphics in sprite slots $E0 through $EF. The 64-byte grid renders as 24-by-21 shapes and smaller components of the story and display sprites.
Last group of common sprite graphics, from VIC slot $F0 to $FE. Some stored shapes have repeated rows and zero padding.

Story interpreter runtime state under the KERNAL jump table. With port $35, sprite commands write shape indices and delay counters here. The instructions at $4589 and $45D6 are RAM writes with this mapping.
Twelve colour bytes read by the story sprite staging loop at $4459 in RAM under the KERNAL.
Thirteen frame hold counters. The shape command clears the selected counter, and the sprite animator decrements nonzero values before fetching another frame.
Thirteen horizontal step bytes in RAM under the KERNAL. Story opcode three writes the selected slot and $4801 adds it to the sprite position.
Thirteen vertical step bytes paired with the horizontal array. $441E clears both arrays when resetting the story sprites.
Six $66 bytes between the story-sprite vertical delta array and the RAM hardware vectors.
The RAM NMI and reset words point to $0D5C in the gameplay image. The IRQ word starts this capture at $0DAE and changes with the raster pass.
